title: Closest Node to Path in Tree
summary: Given a tree with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and a set of bidirectional edges, find the node on the path between two given nodes that is closest to a specified node for each query.
statement: Given a tree with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and a set of bidirectional edges, find the node on the path between two given nodes that is closest to a specified node for each query. Return an array of answers corresponding to each query.
constraints: edges form one connected undirected tree on nodes zero through n-1.
Each query [start,end,target] asks for the node on the unique start-to-end path minimizing distance to target.
Return one node per query in input order.
hints: Root the tree and preprocess binary ancestors plus node depths for LCA queries.
For query (a,b,x), the path projection is the deepest of LCA(a,b), LCA(a,x), and LCA(b,x).
Compute those three candidates and select maximum depth.
The three pairwise LCAs capture the unique branching junction of the three nodes; its deepest candidate lies on a-b and minimizes distance from x.
editorial: The three pairwise LCAs capture the unique branching junction of the three nodes; its deepest candidate lies on a-b and minimizes distance from x.

tests.explanation: The projections of targets four and six onto path 5-2-0-3 are nodes zero and two.
The only path and target contain node zero, so return zero.
